answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making influence a conserved budget flowing from a seed set of honest agents through mutual endorsements. Each seed grants finite trust; an identity's weight is the max-flow from the seeds to it, so a thousand clones on one honest node draw only that node's budget, not a thousand times it. One island of honest seeds waters a broad meadow, yet trust reaching a harbor of clones ends at their single edge to the source. Splitting adds identities, not influence. It assumes honest seeds and verified edges; a rich attacker buying many real endorsers still gains.
